clauses.reason: The order exempts Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age and fixes its own end in the sentence "hereby further exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1940". The exemption therefore ran through September 30, 1940, and that date is recorded as the first end, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends as September 30, 1940 begins) is the alternative, and it would put the end one day earlier. The ending is the order's own stated term and the acting instrument is EO 8252 itself. The only operative sentence is the quoted one; the recital states the finding that the public interest requires the exemption and commands nothing else. The recital says the person had already been exempted under EO 7958 of August 19, 1938; those earlier orders predate this one and cannot end it. Later events recorded for this clause: EO 8543 of September 18, 1940 states "I hereby further exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941"; it cites this order by number, grants a further exemption for a later period, and is recorded as a later event; it does not alter the period stated in this order. Its later-events search lists eo 8543 in an "amended by" disposition note; the later order's own text grants a further exemption and leaves this order's stated period unchanged, so the stated date remains the first end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on "further exempt" orders.

research_rationale:
EO 8252 (1939-09-14, Franklin D. Roosevelt), a one-person exemption from compulsory retirement for age. Text and identity: the held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (common-crawl capture) has the heading "Executive Order 8252—Exemption of Samuel J. Gompers From Compulsory Retirement For Age", which names this order number, its date (1939-09-14) agrees with the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. I read the whole text: one recital and one operative sentence, so the clause inventory is the single whole-paragraph clause. The sentence "hereby further exempt the said Samuel J. Gompers from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1940" fixes the end of the exemption on September 30, 1940; that is the first end, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's later-events search (Federal Register disposition notes of 6938 catalog records from 1937 onward, plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts) returned two hits, notes tying this order to the later further-exemption order EO 8543 and the earlier EO 7958. The packet's name search of held order texts for the person named in this order is also cited. Other leads and later events are discussed in the clause reason. No held source shows an earlier end (revocation, supersession, or an earlier separation or death of the employee), so none is claimed.
